chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ narrated from his uncle Yaʿqūb ibn Sālim, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I have dirhams with me that have images on them, while I am in a state of ihram, so I place them in my money-belt and tie it around my waist.”
He عليه السلام said: “There is no problem. Are they not your expenses, and that upon which you rely after Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?”

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمُ: coins or dirhams used as money
key_terms.تَمَاثِيلُ: images or figures stamped on the coins
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.نَفَقَتَكَ: your travel expenses or financial provision
key_terms.هِمْيَانِي: my money-belt or pouch for carrying expenses

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in ihram to carry coins with images in a money-belt?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling permitting a muhrim to carry coins bearing images in a belt tied around the waist. The Imam عليه السلام explains that this is allowed because such money is needed for one’s travel expenses and livelihood, while ultimate reliance remains upon Allah عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2449 - Ali ibn Asbat narrated from his uncle Ya‘qub ibn Salim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (as), "I have coins with images on them while I am in a state of Ihram. I place them in my belt and tie it around my waist. Is this permissible?"
Imam (as) said: "There is no problem with that. Are they not your expenses upon which you rely after Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious?"
